questions.title: Most Days Above 90°F Per Year
questions.current_disclaimer: Statewide averages derived from NOAA reporting stations. Desert Southwest and Gulf Coast dominate; Alaska and Hawaii have essentially zero.

questions.title: Most Days Below 32°F Per Year
questions.current_disclaimer: Statewide averages from NOAA station normals. Elevation and latitude drive rankings — some interior western states outrank their eastern peers of similar latitude.

questions.title: Most Lightning Strikes Per Square Mile
questions.current_disclaimer: Flash density = cloud-to-ground lightning strikes per square mile per year, averaged across the state. Vaisala NLDN is the standard reference dataset used by NOAA/NWS.

questions.title: Most Severe Thunderstorm Days Per Year
questions.current_disclaimer: A 'severe thunderstorm day' is any calendar day with at least one qualifying severe report in the state (hail >= 1 in, wind >= 58 mph, or tornado). Definition per NOAA SPC.

questions.title: Most Cities Over 100,000 Population
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts only cities that are legally incorporated municipalities; CDPs (census-designated places) and unincorporated communities are excluded.

questions.title: Most Cities Over 500,000 Population
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses incorporated city (not metro area) population.

questions.title: Largest City by Population
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses each state's largest incorporated city (not metro area).

questions.title: Largest State Capital by Population
questions.current_disclaimer: Ranks each state by the population of its designated capital city, not its largest city.

questions.title: Highest Urban Population Share
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses the Census Bureau's 2020 definition of urban areas (≥5,000 people or ≥2,000 housing units in a contiguous developed area).

questions.title: Lowest Urban Population Share
questions.current_disclaimer: Rank 1 = the MOST rural state. Uses the Census 2020 urban-area definition.

questions.title: Tallest Building
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses architectural height (top of spire/roof) per CTBUH, not antenna height. Only completed buildings — under-construction towers excluded.

questions.title: Most Fortune 500 HQ Cities
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts total F500 HQs in the state, not the number of distinct cities that host one.

questions.title: Most Amtrak Stations
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts all active Amtrak-served stations, including thruway bus-only connections at some stops.

questions.title: Largest Metropolitan Area
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses the Census-defined MSA (not CSA / combined). MSAs that cross state lines are credited to the state containing the principal city.

questions.title: Most Cities in the Top 100 by Population
questions.current_disclaimer: Only incorporated cities are counted; CDPs excluded. Ties broken alphabetically for consecutive ranks.

questions.title: Most Colleges in a Single City
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts Title IV degree-granting institutions in a single principal city (not the whole metro). Boston's total is inflated by many small specialty and religious institutions.

questions.title: Longest Ocean Coastline
questions.current_disclaimer: Uses NOAA's 'general coastline' figures (straight-line, excludes bays and river tidal reaches). Great Lakes shorelines excluded — this ranks ocean/tidal coastline only.

questions.title: States Bordering Canada
questions.current_disclaimer: Includes states with a shared land or river border with Canada, ordered by length of shared border in miles. States whose only Canadian boundary is a Great Lake shoreline are excluded.

questions.title: States Bordering Mexico
questions.current_disclaimer: Only 4 states share a land border with Mexico. Ordered by length of shared border.

questions.title: Largest Landlocked States
questions.current_disclaimer: 'Landlocked' here means no ocean coast and no Great Lakes shoreline. States along the Mississippi or other inland rivers still qualify.
